analytic.title: יחסו של הקרא יפת בן עלי לאיסלאם לאור פירושו למזמורי תהילים: יד, נג

biblStruct.note: Reality dictated an ambivalent attitude on the part of the tenth-century Avele Zion (Mourners of Zion) Karaites towards Islam. On the one hand, the Karaites were grateful to Muslim rulers for allowing them to consolidate their movement and disseminate their doctrine throughout the Jewish diaspora. On the other hand, the Avele Zion Karaites viewed Islam as the reign of evil and eagerly awaited its imminent demise. This article examines Yefet Ben Eli's attitude to Islam in the light of his interpretations of Psalms 14 and 53. Yefet considered these psalms as one entity because of their common introduction: "The Unbeliever says in his heart" (Psalms 14:1, 53:2). According to Yefet, the "Unbeliever" in the first psalm refers to Islam, and in the second to Christianity. Yefet even compares the two religions, and concludes that the Christian infidel is infinitely more troublesome for the Jews and further from monotheism than the Muslim one. Therefore, in the End of Days, the Christians will be totally wiped out, while some Muslims will remain and convert to Judaism. This sheds new light on the Karaites' ambivalence toward Islam. Although they were aware of the affinity between Judaism and Islam and the influence that Mu'tazila had on their doctrine, they were unwilling to admit this openly. Yefet alluded to it indirectly, anticipating as he did that the Muslims, who he felt were nearer to Judaism, would assimilate with the Jews in the End of Days.
